upsertSlices.label: Fully dynamic (Δ+1) coloring, adaptive adversary
upsertSlices.task: Maintain an explicit proper vertex coloring after each edge update
assumptions: Maximum degree at most Δ at all times; Δ known in advance
Adaptive adversary; edge insertions and deletions

categories.label: Oblivious · expected and WHP amortized; Δ+1

yAxis.label: Symbolic update-time classes; not a universal asymptotic ranking

parameters.Delta: fixed known maximum degree bound throughout updates
parameters.coordinateConvention: Categorical formula classes and time contracts; no invented numeric exponent.

results.bound: Õ(n^{2/3}); Amortized update time, with high probability
results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Adaptive: updates may depend on past outputs.
results.notes: Uses ordinary O(Δ) recoloring for Δ=O(n^{2/3}). The n^{2/3} discussion in §1.1 is a technique barrier and open question, not a proved dynamic lower bound. Phase initialization is included through amortization; this is not a per-update worst-case guarantee.

results.bound: Õ(n^{8/9}); Amortized update time, with high probability
results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Adaptive: updates may depend on past outputs.
results.notes: Restores the amortized qualifier omitted from the input abstract-only record. FH2025 improves the same adaptive contract. Periodic rebuilding is amortized over phases; §5.4.1 notes sufficiently long sequences for matching initialization.

results.bound: Õ(√n) worst-case update time WHP; at most 3 recolorings
results.guarantee: Maintain a proper (Δ+1)-coloring under adaptive edge insertions and deletions
results.notes: Initially empty graph; subsequent phase preprocessing is pipelined across updates (§4.2). The adaptive adversary may see earlier random bits and internal state. The plotted version fixes a known Δ; §4.4 also supports the maximum degree observed so far. Neither a √n technique barrier nor this algorithm is a maintenance lower bound.

upsertSlices.label: Fully dynamic (Δ+1), oblivious updates
upsertSlices.task: Maintain explicit proper colors after each edge update
assumptions: Update sequence oblivious to algorithmic choices
Edge insertion/deletion; graph maximum degree bounded by Δ

categories.label: Oblivious · expected and WHP amortized; Δ+1

yAxis.label: Symbolic update-time classes; not a universal asymptotic ranking

parameters.Delta: fixed known maximum degree bound throughout updates
parameters.coordinateConvention: Categorical formula classes and time contracts; no invented numeric exponent.

results.bound: O(1)*; Expected and high-probability amortized; O(1) requires t=Ω(n log n+nΔ)
results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Oblivious: update sequence independent of algorithm randomness.
results.notes: The constant marker has a sequence-length footnote. For shorter sequences retain the additive n log n+nΔ overhead; this is not constant expected time at every update position. For t updates: total O(n log n+nΔ+t); space O(nΔ+m_max). Initially empty graph.

results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Oblivious: update sequence independent of algorithm randomness.
results.notes: The source writes O(log Δ); log⁺Δ=max{1,log Δ} covers trivial constant-degree cases. §6 treats changing Δ separately; this comparison fixes Δ. The paper's amortized convention starts with an empty graph. Main fixed-Δ version shown.

results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Oblivious: update sequence independent of algorithm randomness.
results.notes: Independent constant-time approach. It is a separate theorem from BGKLS2022 with a different time guarantee; both original records remain visible. Empty-graph initialization with independently sampled vertex ranks; preprocessing is distinct from update cost.

results.bound: O(1); Expected worst-case per-update time; not amortized
results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; Δ+1 colors; Oblivious: update sequence independent of algorithm randomness.
results.notes: Worst-case refers to the update position before expectation over random choices. This is neither a deterministic nor a high-probability O(1) bound, nor a conditional expectation for every realized random history. O(n) initialization. §3 restarts on rare failures to remove the polynomial sequence-length restriction without changing O(1) expectation.

upsertSlices.label: Deterministic dynamic degree-based palette
upsertSlices.task: Maintain explicit colors after edge insertion/deletion

categories.label: Oblivious · expected and WHP amortized; Δ+1

yAxis.label: Symbolic update-time classes; not a universal asymptotic ranking

parameters.Delta: fixed known maximum degree bound throughout updates
parameters.coordinateConvention: Categorical formula classes and time contracts; no invented numeric exponent.

results.bound: O(polylog Δ); Deterministic amortized update time
results.guarantee: Explicit proper vertex coloring maintained after every edge insertion or deletion; (1+o(1))Δ colors; Arbitrary updates; deterministic algorithm permits adaptive choices.
results.notes: The o(1) tends to zero as Δ grows. This palette family is not an ε tradeoff and does not promise Δ+1 colors. Constant-degree cases use ordinary O(Δ) updates. Determinism permits updates based on past outputs. Initially empty graph under the paper's amortization convention.
